# Table

> Rows and columns, laid out and announced like a native table, that components can render into. Column headers can be buttons that sort.

`<slab-table>` · Data · built on `[role=table] + rowgroups, rows and cells`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/table/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/table.js';
import 'slab-elements/table.head.js';
import 'slab-elements/table.body.js';
import 'slab-elements/table.foot.js';
import 'slab-elements/table.row.js';
import 'slab-elements/table.column-header.js';
import 'slab-elements/table.cell.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<h2 id="caption">Pours</h2>

<slab-table aria-labelledby="caption">
  <slab-table-head>
    <slab-table-row>
      <slab-table-column-header sortable sort="ascending"
        >Slab</slab-table-column-header
      >
      <slab-table-column-header sortable>Yards</slab-table-column-header>
    </slab-table-row>
  </slab-table-head>
  <slab-table-body>
    <slab-table-row>
      <slab-table-cell row-header>Driveway</slab-table-cell>
      <slab-table-cell>12</slab-table-cell>
    </slab-table-row>
    <slab-table-row>
      <slab-table-cell row-header>Patio</slab-table-cell>
      <slab-table-cell>8</slab-table-cell>
    </slab-table-row>
  </slab-table-body>
</slab-table>
```

A native `<table>` can only hold its own elements, so a component that renders a row or a cell can't go in one. Table and its parts can. Each is laid out as the element it stands for, `display: table-row` for a Table Row and so on, so columns size to fit their content and line up across the head, body and foot, and each has that element's role. Table Head goes first and Table Foot last, wherever they are in the markup.

Name the Table as you would a native one, with `aria-labelledby` pointing at a heading or caption near it, or with `aria-label`. Give the Cell that says what a row is about, such as a name, `row-header`, and it becomes the row's header, like a `<th scope="row">`, so a screenreader moving down a column reads each Cell with it.

A `sortable` Column Header is a `<button>`. Clicking it sorts its column ascending, or descending when it's already ascending, sets `sort`, and dispatches "sort" from the Column Header. Every other Column Header in its Table goes back to `sort="none"` first, so only one column is sorted, and only it has `aria-sort`. Screenreaders are told how it's sorted, "Sorted by Yards, descending", which you can word with `sortedLabel` or `tableSorted` in `registerStrings()`. Put an arrow in its `sort-indicator` slot, or draw one on `:state(ascending)` and `:state(descending)`.

Sorting the rows is yours, since Table doesn't move them: on "sort", put the Table Body's rows in the order the Column Header's `sort` says, as the example above does, or sort your data and let your framework render it. Set `sort` yourself for a Table that starts out sorted.

It's a table, not a grid. It's read, not moved through with the arrow keys, and only a sortable Column Header's button and what you put in a Cell take focus. Cells can't span columns or rows.

## Keyboard

| Key          | What it does                                                       |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tab          | Moves to each sortable Column Header, then to what's in the Cells. |
| Enter, Space | On a sortable Column Header, sorts its column.                     |

## Elements

### `<slab-table>`

Import `slab-elements/table.js` to register it.

A Table with no visual styles: a `[role=table]` of rows and columns, laid out like a native `<table>`, with Column Headers that can sort.

A native `<table>` can only hold its own elements, so a component that renders rows or cells can't go in one. Table and its parts can: a Table Head, Body and Foot, each with Table Rows, which hold Column Headers or Cells. Each is laid out as the element it stands for, so columns size to fit their content, and each has that element's role.

Name the Table with `aria-labelledby`, pointing at a heading or caption near it, or with `aria-label`.

Clicking a `sortable` Column Header sorts its column and dispatches "sort" from it. Table makes every other Column Header unsorted first, so only one column is sorted at a time. Sorting the rows is yours.

It's a table, not a grid: it's read rather than moved through with the arrow keys, and the only things in it that take focus are a sortable Column Header's button and whatever you put in a Cell.

#### Properties

| Name                        | Type                  | Description                   |
| --------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `columnHeaders` (read-only) | `TableColumnHeader[]` | Its Column Headers, in order. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                                  | Description                   |
| --------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| (default) | `TableBody \| TableFoot \| TableHead` | The Table Head, Body and Foot |

### `<slab-table-head>`

Import `slab-elements/table.head.js` to register it.

A Table Head with no visual styles: a `[role=rowgroup]` around the header rows, such as the row of Column Headers. It goes first in its Table, wherever it is in the markup, as a `<thead>` does.

#### Slots

| Name      | Type       | Description     |
| --------- | ---------- | --------------- |
| (default) | `TableRow` | The header rows |

### `<slab-table-body>`

Import `slab-elements/table.body.js` to register it.

A Table Body with no visual styles: a `[role=rowgroup]` around the body rows, holding the data.

#### Slots

| Name      | Type       | Description   |
| --------- | ---------- | ------------- |
| (default) | `TableRow` | The body rows |

### `<slab-table-foot>`

Import `slab-elements/table.foot.js` to register it.

A Table Foot with no visual styles: a `[role=rowgroup]` around the footer rows, such as totals. It goes last in its Table, wherever it is in the markup, as a `<tfoot>` does.

#### Slots

| Name      | Type       | Description     |
| --------- | ---------- | --------------- |
| (default) | `TableRow` | The footer rows |

### `<slab-table-row>`

Import `slab-elements/table.row.js` to register it.

A Table Row with no visual styles: a `[role=row]` of Column Headers or Cells, in a Table Head, Body or Foot.

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                             | Description                            |
| --------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| (default) | `TableCell \| TableColumnHeader` | The row's Cells, or its Column Headers |

### `<slab-table-column-header>`

Import `slab-elements/table.column-header.js` to register it.

A Table Column Header with no visual styles: a `[role=columnheader]` that names its column, in a Table Head's row.

With `sortable`, its content is a `<button>`. Clicking it sorts the column ascending, or descending when it's already ascending, sets `sort` and dispatches "sort". Its Table sets every other Column Header's `sort` to "none", so only one column is sorted at a time, and screenreaders are told how it's sorted now.

Sorting the rows is yours: on "sort", put the Table Body's rows in the order `sort` says. Slab doesn't move them, so a framework that renders the rows stays in charge of them.

`aria-sort` follows `sort`, and is left off while it's "none", since only the sorted column should have it. Set `sort` yourself for a Table that starts out sorted.

Style it through its parts and `:state(ascending)`, `:state(descending)` and `:state(sortable)`.

#### Attributes

| Name       | Type                                    | Default  | Description                                             |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sort`     | `'ascending' \| 'descending' \| 'none'` | `'none'` | How the column is sorted. Sets `aria-sort`.             |
| `sortable` | `boolean`                               | `false`  | Makes the Column Header a button that sorts the column. |

#### Properties

| Name          | Type                                                            | Description                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sortedLabel` | `(column: string, sort: 'ascending' \| 'descending') => string` | What screenreaders are told when the user sorts the column, from its name and `sort`. "Sorted by", the name and the direction in English when unset. |

#### Events

| Name   | Type    | Description                                                                         |
| ------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sort` | `Event` | When the user presses the button to sort by its column. Set `sort` in your handler. |

#### Slots

| Name             | Type                | Description                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| (default)        | `Element \| string` | The column's name                                                                                 |
| `sort-indicator` | `Element \| string` | Shown after the name in a sortable Column Header, such as an arrow, and hidden from screenreaders |

#### CSS parts

| Name             | Description                                                                     |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`          | Holds the name in a sortable Column Header                                      |
| `sort-button`    | The button in a sortable Column Header                                          |
| `sort-indicator` | Holds the sort indicator in a sortable Column Header, hidden from screenreaders |

#### CSS states

| Name                 | Description                                  |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(ascending)`  | While the table is sorted by it, ascending.  |
| `:state(descending)` | While the table is sorted by it, descending. |
| `:state(sortable)`   | While it's `sortable`.                       |

### `<slab-table-cell>`

Import `slab-elements/table.cell.js` to register it.

A Table Cell with no visual styles: a `[role=cell]` in a Table Row, or a `[role=rowheader]` with `row-header`.

A row header names its row, as a Column Header names its column, so a screenreader moving down a column reads each Cell with its row's header. Make the Cell that says what the row is about, such as a name, the row header.

#### Attributes

| Name         | Type      | Default | Description                                                 |
| ------------ | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `row-header` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the Cell its row's header, like a `<th scope="row">`. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description        |
| --------- | ------------------- | ------------------ |
| (default) | `Element \| string` | The Cell's content |
